title: Clinical Nurse Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate your clinical nurse salary from hourly rates under the Nurses Award. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates.
salarySummary: For an Occupational Health Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1 under the Nurses Award, the hourly rate is $34.45, leading to an annual salary of approximately $68,073 based on a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: What is the hourly rate for a clinical nurse under the Nurses Award?
faqs.a: Under the Nurses Award [MA000034], clinical nurse roles such as Occupational Health Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1 have a minimum hourly rate of $34.45 as of the first full pay period on or after 1 August 2026. Rates vary by classification and pay point, with higher levels earning up to $71.23 per hour for a Registered Nurse Level 5 Grade 6. Always check the latest pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman for your specific role.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a clinical nurse salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Nurses Award receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, an Occupational Health Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1 with a base rate of $34.45 would have a casual rate of $43.06 per hour. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave. Use our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) tool to calculate it.

faqs.q: What tax and superannuation should I expect on my clinical nurse salary?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates start at nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2%. Superannuation is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a personalised estimate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you’re a nurse or considering a nursing career, understanding your **clinical nurse salary** is essential for budgeting and negotiating. Whether you’re offered an hourly rate or an annual figure, converting between the two helps you compare jobs and plan your finances. This guide uses the latest rates from the Nurses Award [MA000034] and explains how to calculate your annual pay, fortnightly pay, tax, and superannuation.

## Understanding the clinical nurse salary under the Nurses Award

The Nurses Award covers most nurses in Australia, including registered nurses, enrolled nurses, and occupational health nurses. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides with minimum rates for each classification. For example, an Occupational Health Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1 earns **$34.45 per hour** as of the first full pay period on or after 1 August 2026. This is well above the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, reflecting the skilled nature of nursing.

Award rates are legally enforceable minimums. Some employers may pay above the award, but never below. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database also provides detailed spreadsheets for all awards.

### Hourly to annual conversion

The standard formula for converting an hourly rate to annual salary is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For full-time nurses under the Nurses Award, the ordinary hours are 38 per week. Using the Occupational Health Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1 rate:

$34.45 × 38 × 52 = **$68,073.20 per year**

This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work part-time, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. For casual employees, remember that the 25% casual loading is already included in the casual hourly rate shown in the pay guide. Never add casual loading on top of a rate that already includes it. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool can help you run the numbers.

### Fortnightly pay

Many nurses are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by two:

$34.45 × 38 = $1,309.10 per week
$1,309.10 × 2 = **$2,618.20 per fortnight**

This figure is useful for budgeting and comparing with salary offers that are quoted fortnightly. The [pay guides](/blog) page has more examples for different classifications.

### Tax and Medicare

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your tax. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a clinical nurse salary of $68,073, the tax would be approximately:

- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($45,000 – $18,200) = $4,020
- 30% on $23,073 ($68,073 – $45,000) = $6,921.90
- Total tax = $10,941.90
- Medicare levy (2% of $68,073) = $1,361.46
- Total tax and Medicare = **$12,303.36**

This leaves an after-tax annual income of about $55,770. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a more precise estimate that includes your specific circumstances.

### Superannuation

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is **12% of ordinary earnings**, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For our example:

$68,073 × 12% = **$8,168.76 per year** in super contributions

This is not deducted from your salary; your employer pays it into your super fund. If you earn above the maximum base, super only applies to the first $270,830. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice can affect your take-home pay.

## Other considerations for clinical nurse salary

- **Casual loading**: If you’re casual, your base rate includes 25% loading. For Occupational Health Nurse Level 1 Pay Point 1, the casual rate is $43.06 per hour. Annualise that: $43.06 × 38 × 52 = $85,086.56. Remember, casual employees don’t get paid leave, so the loading compensates for that.
- **Penalty rates**: The Nurses Award provides higher pay for Saturday, Sunday, and public holidays. For example, Saturday rate is 150% of the base rate. These are not included in the simple annual conversion.
- **Allowances**: You may be entitled to laundry, uniform, on-call, or vehicle allowances. The pay guide lists these separately.
- **Enterprise agreements**: If your workplace has an enterprise agreement, it may override the award. Always check your agreement first.

## Conclusion

Knowing your **clinical nurse salary** in both hourly and annual terms empowers you to make informed career decisions. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 for full-time work, and remember that tax, Medicare, and super are additional layers. For the most accurate figures, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides and the ATO’s tax tables. Our [reference tables](/data) provide a quick look at minimum wages and award rates.
